metadata.title: Screen Capture - Screenshot Tool
metadata.description: Capture any area of your screen, add annotations, and download as PNG. One click, no URL needed, nothing uploaded.

scroll-capture.title: Screen Capture
scroll-capture.description: Capture any area of your screen, add annotations, and download as PNG. One click, no URL needed, nothing uploaded.

faqs.question: How does this tool work?
faqs.answer: Click Start Screen Capture, choose the screen, window, or tab to capture in the browser dialog, then drag a box on the preview to select the area. You can annotate it with shapes, arrows, text, or mosaic before saving.

faqs.question: Can I capture only part of the screen?
faqs.answer: Yes. After the capture starts, drag on the preview to choose any rectangular area. Everything outside the box is excluded.

faqs.question: Can I annotate the screenshot?
faqs.answer: Yes. A toolbar offers pencil, shapes (rectangle, circle, arrow), text, and mosaic. You can undo any step with Ctrl+Z.

faqs.question: Why does the browser ask for screen sharing?
faqs.answer: The tool uses your browser's built-in screen capture, so the system asks you to choose which screen, window, or tab to share. Your image is processed entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

faqs.question: Does it work on mobile?
faqs.answer: Screen capture requires a desktop browser with getDisplayMedia support (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari on desktop). It is not available on mobile browsers.

intro.line1: Capture any area of your screen — no URLs, no uploads.
steps: Click Start Screen Capture and choose the screen, window, or tab to capture.
Drag on the preview to select the area, or keep it as the full screen.
Annotate with pencil, shapes, arrows, text, or mosaic if you like.
Click the checkmark to finish and download the PNG.

scroll-capture.startHint: Click the button, then choose what to capture in the browser dialog.

whatIs.title: What Is Screen Capture?
body: Screen Capture takes a picture of any part of your screen using your browser's built-in capture API. You can crop to the area you need and add annotations before saving. Everything stays in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

howTo.title: How to Take a Screenshot
items: Click Start Screen Capture and pick the screen, window, or tab to share in the system dialog.
Drag a rectangle on the preview to crop, or keep the whole screen.
Use the toolbar to annotate: pencil, rectangle, circle, arrow, text, or mosaic.
Click the checkmark to confirm and download the PNG, or press Esc to cancel.

tips.title: Tips
items: Press Ctrl+Z to undo the last annotation step.
The result is copied to your clipboard automatically on supported browsers.
For long pages, scroll to the area you want before capturing — this tool captures what is on screen.

errors.notSupported: Your browser does not support screen capture (getDisplayMedia).
errors.permissionDenied: Screen capture permission was denied. Please allow access and try again.
errors.startFailed: Could not start screen capture. Please try again.

metadata.title: Video to GIF Converter - Free Online Tool
metadata.description: Convert any video to an animated GIF. Trim, resize, and adjust frame rate. No upload, runs in your browser.

video-to-gif.title: Video to GIF Converter
video-to-gif.description: Convert any video to an animated GIF. Trim, resize, and adjust frame rate. No upload, runs in your browser.

faqs.question: What video formats are supported?
faqs.answer: Any format your browser can play — MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, and more. MP4 (H.264) has the best compatibility.

faqs.question: Is there a file size limit?
faqs.answer: No hard limit. Large videos use more RAM since processing happens in your browser. For best results, trim to a short clip before converting.

faqs.question: How do I make the GIF smaller?
faqs.answer: Reduce the width (pixels), lower the FPS, and shorten the duration. A 480px wide, 10fps, 3-second GIF is typically under 2MB.

faqs.question: Why does my GIF look grainy?
faqs.answer: GIFs are limited to 256 colors per frame. Complex scenes with many colors will show banding. Simpler scenes with fewer colors convert better.

faqs.question: Is my video uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser using the Canvas API. Your video never leaves your device.

whatIs.title: What Is the Video to GIF Converter?
body: Turn any video file into an animated GIF right in your browser. Trim the clip, choose the output width, set the frame rate, and download the result.

howTo.title: How to Convert Video to GIF
items: Upload or drop a video file (MP4, WebM, MOV).
Set the start and end times to trim the clip.
Choose the output width and frames per second.
Click Convert to GIF and download.

tips.title: Tips
items: Lower the width and FPS to reduce GIF file size.
Keep clips short for faster processing and smaller files.
GIFs support 256 colors per frame; simple scenes look best.

metadata.title: Image to GIF Maker - Free Online Tool
metadata.description: Turn images into an animated GIF. Add multiple photos, set frame delay and size, and reorder frames. No upload, runs in your browser.

image-to-gif.title: Image to GIF Maker
image-to-gif.description: Turn images into an animated GIF. Add multiple photos, set frame delay and size, and reorder frames. No upload, runs in your browser.

faqs.question: What image formats are supported?
faqs.answer: PNG, JPG, WEBP, BMP, and more. You can also drag and drop an existing GIF — its frames are automatically extracted and added to your animation.

faqs.question: Can I add multiple images?
faqs.answer: Yes. Upload as many images as you like, then reorder, remove, or preview each frame before generating the GIF.

faqs.question: How do I control the animation speed?
faqs.answer: Use the delay slider, measured in milliseconds. A lower value makes the animation faster; a higher value slows it down.

faqs.question: Why does my GIF look grainy?
faqs.answer: GIFs are limited to 256 colors per frame. Photos with smooth gradients will show banding. Flat-color images and graphics convert best.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser using the Canvas API. Your images never leave your device.

upload.drop: Drop images or click to upload

whatIs.title: What Is the Image to GIF Maker?
body: Combine multiple pictures into an animated GIF right in your browser. Add frames, set the delay between them, pick the output size, and download your animation.

howTo.title: How to Make a GIF from Images
items: Drop or upload one or more images (PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF).
Reorder or remove frames as needed.
Set the frame delay and output width and height.
Click Generate GIF, then download the result.

tips.title: Tips
items: Keep the animation short — fewer frames make smaller files.
Reduce the width to shrink file size while keeping quality.
Use consistent image sizes for smoother animations.

gif-to-images.title: GIF to Images Splitter
gif-to-images.description: Extract all frames from a GIF as individual images. Export each frame as PNG, WEBP, or JPEG, or download all frames as a ZIP. No upload, runs in your browser.

faqs.question: How do I extract frames from a GIF?
faqs.answer: Drop your GIF into the upload area. Every frame is decoded locally and shown as a thumbnail. Click a frame to download it, or download all frames as a ZIP.

faqs.question: Which export formats are available?
faqs.answer: PNG (lossless, recommended), WEBP, and JPEG. Pick a format before downloading frames.

faqs.question: Will transparent backgrounds be preserved?
faqs.answer: Yes. PNG and WEBP export keep transparency. JPEG does not support transparency and will flatten the background.

faqs.question: Is my GIF uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The GIF is decoded entirely in your browser. Your file never leaves your device.

whatIs.title: What Is the GIF to Images Splitter?
body: Break an animated GIF into its individual frames. Each frame is extracted locally, previewed as a thumbnail, and can be saved as PNG, WEBP, or JPEG — individually or all at once as a ZIP.

howTo.title: How to Split a GIF into Images
items: Drop or upload a GIF file.
Wait for the frames to be decoded.
Choose PNG, WEBP, or JPEG as the export format.
Download frames individually or all at once as a ZIP.

tips.title: Tips
items: PNG is lossless and keeps transparency — best for editing.
Use WEBP when you need smaller files without losing transparency.
JPEG works well for stills from video-like GIFs, but has no transparency.

metadata.title: Screen Color Picker - Free Online Tool
metadata.description: Pick any color from your screen with one click. No image upload needed. Copy Hex, RGB, and HSL values instantly. Works in Chrome, Edge, and Safari.

screen-color-picker.title: Screen Color Picker
screen-color-picker.description: Click a button, then click anywhere on your screen — including other apps — to grab the exact color. Copy it as Hex, RGB, or HSL instantly. No image upload, no signup.

faqs.question: Can I pick colors outside the browser window?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool uses your system's built-in eyedropper, so you can click anywhere on your screen — including other applications, the taskbar, or your wallpaper — and it will return the exact color.

faqs.question: Why is the button disabled for me?
faqs.answer: The eyedropper requires the browser's EyeDropper API, supported by Chrome, Edge, Opera, and Safari 17.2+. Firefox and some older browsers don't support it yet — switch to Chrome, Edge, or a recent Safari to use this tool.

faqs.question: Is the color data sent anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your picked colors are only stored in your browser's localStorage so your recent picks persist between visits — they are never transmitted.

faqs.question: What's the difference from Image Color Picker?
faqs.answer: Image Color Picker samples colors inside an uploaded picture. This screen picker grabs colors from your actual display without any upload — use it when you want to match a color you see anywhere on your screen.

faqs.question: How do I copy a color?
faqs.answer: After picking, the current color shows Hex, RGB, and HSL values, each with a one-click copy button. Your recent picks appear below as swatches you can click to recall.

guide.heading: How to use:
steps: Click "Pick Color from Screen".
Click anywhere on your screen to sample a color.
Copy the Hex, RGB, or HSL value with one click.
Your recent picks are saved for the next visit.

ui.hint: Click the button, then click anywhere on your screen — other windows included.
ui.unsupported: Your browser doesn't support screen color picking. Please use Chrome, Edge, Opera, or Safari 17.2+.

metadata.title: Multiavatar Avatar Generator - Free Online Tool
metadata.description: Generate a unique multicultural avatar from any text. 12+ billion combinations, works fully in your browser. Download as SVG or PNG — no upload, no signup.

multiavatar-avatar-generator.title: Multiavatar Avatar Generator
multiavatar-avatar-generator.description: Generate a unique multicultural avatar from any text. Every string produces its own distinct avatar — perfect for profile pictures, gaming logos, and identicons. Runs entirely in your browser.

faqs.question: Does the same text always produce the same avatar?
faqs.answer: Yes. Multiavatar works like an identicon — the text is hashed into a set of numbers that pick the avatar's parts. Type the same text again and you get the exact same avatar every time.

faqs.question: Are my avatars uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. The generator runs entirely in your browser using a small client-side library. Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere, and no data is stored.

faqs.question: Can I use the generated avatars commercially?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Multiavatar library is free for commercial use. Generated avatars may be used on websites, apps, products, and social profiles without restriction.

faqs.question: What download formats are available?
faqs.answer: SVG for a scalable vector image (crisp at any size) and PNG at 512x512 for easy use on websites, apps, and social profiles. Toggle "Remove background circle" for a head-only avatar.

faqs.question: How many unique avatars exist?
faqs.answer: The algorithm combines 48 base designs into 48^6 = 12,230,590,464 possible avatars. Some parts are intentionally similar, but every text string maps to its own distinct avatar.

guide.heading: How to use:
steps: Type any text — your name, username, or a random string.
Watch the avatar update instantly. Hit "Shuffle" for a random one.
Optionally remove the background circle.
Download as SVG or PNG.

ui.placeholder: Type any text to create your avatar…
ui.hint: The same text always generates the same avatar — like a fingerprint for your name.

video-compressor.title: Video Compressor
video-compressor.description: Compress video files for free. Reduce MP4, WebM, and MOV file size with adjustable quality. No upload, no signup — runs entirely in your browser.

faqs.question: How much can I compress a video?
faqs.answer: Typically 50-90% reduction depending on the original quality and your compression settings. A 100 MB video can often be reduced to 10-30 MB at medium quality with little visible difference.

faqs.question: Does compressing a video reduce quality?
faqs.answer: Some quality loss is inherent in compression, but at medium-high settings the difference is barely noticeable. The tool lets you preview the result before downloading so you can find the right balance.

faqs.question: What video formats are supported?
faqs.answer: Upload MP4, WebM, or MOV files. The compressed output is always MP4 (H.264) which is universally compatible with all devices and platforms.

faqs.question: Is my video uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All compression happens locally in your browser using FFmpeg WebAssembly. Your video never leaves your device. Nothing is stored anywhere.

faqs.question: Why is compression slow?
faqs.answer: Video encoding is CPU-intensive work. Processing happens in your browser via WebAssembly, which is slower than native software. Shorter videos and lower resolutions process faster.

faqs.question: Can I compress videos for email or Discord?
faqs.answer: Yes. Email typically limits attachments to 25 MB, Discord free tier to 25 MB. Use medium or high compression to get your video under these limits.

guide.heading: How to use:
steps: Upload your video file (MP4, WebM, MOV).
Choose quality level and target resolution.
Click "Compress Video" and wait for processing.
Download your compressed video.

resume-builder.title: Resume Builder
resume-builder.description: Build a professional resume for free. Choose a template, fill in your details, and download as PDF. No signup required.

faqs.question: Is this resume builder completely free?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% free with no limits. Build and download unlimited resumes. No signup, no watermark, no hidden fees. Everything runs in your browser.

faqs.question: How do I download my resume as a PDF?
faqs.answer: Click 'Download PDF' and your browser's print dialog will open. Select 'Save as PDF' as the destination. This preserves the exact layout and formatting of your resume.

faqs.question: Is my data safe?
faqs.answer: Your resume data never leaves your device. Everything is processed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded to any server. Close the tab and all data is gone.

faqs.question: What resume format should I use?
faqs.answer: For most job applications, a reverse-chronological format works best — list your most recent experience first. The Classic and Modern templates both use this format. Use Minimal for creative roles or when you want a clean, simple look.

faqs.question: Can I use this resume for ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems)?
faqs.answer: Yes. All templates output clean, readable text that ATS systems can parse. Avoid using images or complex graphics in your resume content for best ATS compatibility.

faqs.question: How long should my resume be?
faqs.answer: One page for early-career professionals (0-10 years). Two pages are acceptable for senior roles with extensive experience. Keep it concise — recruiters spend an average of 6-7 seconds on initial resume screening.

guide.heading: How to use:
steps: Choose a template style (Classic, Modern, or Minimal).
Fill in your personal details, summary, experience, education, and skills.
Preview your resume in the right panel.
Click "Download PDF" to save your resume.

metadata.title: Video Watermark Remover
metadata.description: Remove watermarks from videos of any length. No time limits, no upload, free forever.

video-watermark-remover.title: Video Watermark Remover
video-watermark-remover.description: Remove watermarks from any video for free. Smart Remove and Blur modes. No upload, no signup, runs entirely in your browser.

faqs.question: How do I remove a watermark from a video for free?
faqs.answer: Upload your video to this tool, draw a rectangle over the watermark, choose Smart Remove or Blur mode, and click Remove Watermark. Everything runs in your browser — no upload, no signup.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Smart Remove and Blur?
faqs.answer: Smart Remove uses FFmpeg's delogo filter to intelligently interpolate surrounding pixels into the watermark area, producing natural-looking results. Blur applies a heavy Gaussian blur that completely obscures the watermark — useful when Smart Remove leaves artifacts on complex backgrounds.

faqs.question: Does removing a video watermark reduce quality?
faqs.answer: The tool uses FFmpeg with high-quality encoding (CRF 20) so the rest of your video stays sharp. Only the selected watermark region is modified. Audio is copied without re-encoding.

faqs.question: Is there a file size or video length limit?
faqs.answer: There is no hard limit since all processing happens locally in your browser. Smart Remove and Blur both handle long videos efficiently.

faqs.question: Can I remove watermarks from TikTok or YouTube videos?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as you have the video file downloaded. Upload the MP4, WebM, or MOV file and select the watermark area.

faqs.question: Is my video uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser using WebAssembly-powered FFmpeg. Your video never leaves your device.

whatIs.title: What Is the Video Watermark Remover?
whatIs.body: The Video Watermark Remover is a free browser-based tool that removes watermarks, logos, and text overlays from any video file. It uses FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, running entirely in your browser with no server uploads.

modes.title: Two Removal Modes
items: Smart Remove — Uses FFmpeg's delogo filter to interpolate surrounding pixels into the watermark area. Fast and effective for most watermarks, especially on simple or uniform backgrounds.
Blur — Applies a heavy Gaussian blur that completely obscures the watermark. Use when Smart Remove leaves artifacts, or when the watermark is on a very complex moving background.

howTo.title: How to Remove a Watermark
items: Upload your video file (MP4, WebM, MOV).
Scrub the timeline to find a frame where the watermark is visible.
Click and drag a rectangle tightly around the watermark.
Choose Smart Remove or Blur.
Click Remove Watermark and wait for processing.
Preview the result and download.

tips.title: Tips for Best Results
items: Draw the rectangle as tightly as possible — a smaller selection produces cleaner results.
Smart Remove works best for semi-transparent stock watermarks and text on uniform backgrounds.
Use Blur as a fallback when Smart Remove leaves visible artifacts.

metadata.title: Photo Watermark Remover
metadata.description: Remove watermarks from photos for free. No signup, no limits, 100% private.

photo-watermark-remover.title: Photo Watermark Remover
photo-watermark-remover.description: Remove watermarks from photos completely free. No signup, no limits. Your image never leaves your browser — all processing happens locally.

faqs.question: How do I remove a watermark from a photo for free?
faqs.answer: Upload your image, paint over the watermark with the brush tool (it appears as a red overlay), and click Remove Watermark. The tool uses an inpainting algorithm to fill the area with surrounding pixel data. Everything runs locally in your browser.

faqs.question: Does removing a photo watermark affect image quality?
faqs.answer: The inpainting algorithm only modifies the pixels you paint over. The rest of the image remains completely untouched. You can download the result at full original resolution as a PNG file.

faqs.question: What image formats are supported?
faqs.answer: The tool accepts PNG, JPG, JPEG, WebP, and any other image format your browser supports. The output is always downloaded as a high-quality PNG file regardless of the input format.

faqs.question: Can I remove text overlays and logos from photos?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paint over any text, logo, or graphic overlay with the brush and the inpainting algorithm will attempt to reconstruct the background behind it. Results work best on photos with relatively uniform or textured backgrounds.

faqs.question: Is there a maximum image size I can process?
faqs.answer: There is no hard limit, but very large images (over 8000px) may be slow to process since the inpainting runs on the CPU in your browser. For best performance, images under 4000px wide work smoothly.

faqs.question: Is my photo uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser. Your image never leaves your device, so your photos stay completely private.

whatIs.title: What Is the Photo Watermark Remover?
body: The Photo Watermark Remover is a free online tool that removes watermarks, logos, text overlays, and other unwanted objects from images. It uses an inpainting algorithm that reconstructs the area behind the watermark based on surrounding pixel data.
Everything runs locally in your browser. Your photos are never uploaded to any server, which means your images stay completely private and processing is instant.

howTo.title: How to Remove a Watermark from a Photo
howTo.intro: Removing a watermark takes just a few steps:
items: Upload your image by clicking the upload area or dragging and dropping a file (PNG, JPG, or WebP).
Adjust the brush size using the slider or the keyboard shortcuts: press [ to decrease and ] to increase.
Paint over the watermark area. A red overlay shows what you have selected.
Click Remove Watermark to process the image.
Review the result and download your clean image as a full-resolution PNG.

algorithm.title: How the Inpainting Algorithm Works
algorithm.body: The tool uses a pixel-based inpainting technique that analyzes the colors and textures around the masked area. It progressively fills in pixels from the boundary inward, sampling nearby regions to reconstruct a natural-looking background. This approach works especially well on textured surfaces, gradients, and photographs with organic patterns.

tips.title: Tips for Best Results
items: Use a brush size that closely matches the thickness of the watermark text or logo for precise coverage.
Paint slightly beyond the edges of the watermark to catch semi-transparent pixels.
For large watermarks covering complex areas, process in smaller sections — paint and remove one area at a time.
Results are best on photos with textured or varied backgrounds. Watermarks over faces or fine detail may require touch-up.

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Removing stock photo watermarks after purchasing a license.
Cleaning up screenshots with unwanted text overlays.
Removing date stamps from scanned photos.
Erasing logos or branding from product images.
Preparing images for presentations and portfolios.

metadata.title: QR Code Generator
metadata.description: Generate customizable QR codes from any text or URL

qr-code-generator.title: QR Code Generator
qr-code-generator.description: Generate customizable QR codes from any text or URL. Adjust size, colors, and error correction level.

faqs.question: How do I create a QR code for a URL?
faqs.answer: Paste your URL into the text field and the QR code generates instantly. You can customize the size, colors, and error correction level, then download it as a PNG or copy it to your clipboard.

faqs.question: What is QR code error correction and which level should I use?
faqs.answer: Error correction allows a QR code to be scanned even if part of it is damaged or obscured. Medium (15%) is a good default. Use High (30%) if you plan to place a logo over the QR code or print it on materials that may get scratched.

faqs.question: Can I customize the colors of my QR code?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can set both the foreground and background colors using the color pickers or by entering hex values directly. Make sure there is enough contrast between the two colors for scanners to read the code reliably.

faqs.question: What is the maximum amount of data a QR code can hold?
faqs.answer: A QR code can store up to about 4,296 alphanumeric characters or 7,089 numeric digits. For practical use, URLs under 500 characters work best and produce QR codes that are easy to scan.

faqs.question: Is this QR code generator free to use?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is completely free with no signup required. The QR codes are generated in your browser and there are no limits on how many you can create or download.

faqs.question: Can I use the generated QR codes for commercial purposes?
faqs.answer: Yes. The QR codes you generate are yours to use however you like, including on printed materials, products, business cards, and marketing campaigns. There are no restrictions.

whatIs.title: What Is the QR Code Generator?
body: This QR Code Generator lets you create customizable QR codes from any text or URL instantly. You can adjust the output size, foreground and background colors, and error correction level. The generated QR code can be downloaded as a PNG image or copied directly to your clipboard.
QR codes are two-dimensional barcodes that can be scanned by smartphones and dedicated readers. They are widely used for sharing URLs, contact information, Wi-Fi credentials, and other data quickly.

howTo.title: How to Create a QR Code
howTo.intro: Creating a QR code takes seconds:
items: Type or paste your text or URL into the input field. The QR code generates automatically as you type.
Choose a size from the dropdown (128px to 1024px).
Select an error correction level. Medium (15%) is the recommended default.
Optionally customize the foreground and background colors using the color pickers.
Click Download PNG to save the image, or Copy Image to place it on your clipboard.

errorCorrection.title: Understanding Error Correction Levels
errorCorrection.body: QR codes include redundant data that allows them to be read even when partially damaged. The four error correction levels determine how much damage a code can tolerate:
items: Low (7%) — Smallest code size, least redundancy. Use when the QR code will always be displayed on a clean screen.
Medium (15%) — Good balance of size and reliability. Best for most use cases.
Quartile (25%) — Higher redundancy. Good for printed materials that may get scratched.
High (30%) — Maximum redundancy. Required if you plan to overlay a logo on the QR code.

tips.title: Tips for Creating Effective QR Codes
items: Keep your URLs short. Shorter data produces simpler QR codes that scan faster and more reliably.
Maintain high contrast between foreground and background colors. Dark on light is most reliable.
Test your QR code on multiple devices before printing or publishing.
Use at least 256px for print materials and 512px or larger for posters and signage.

items: Business cards linking to a website or contact page.
Restaurant menus accessible via table QR codes.
Event tickets and check-in systems.
Product packaging linking to instructions or warranty registration.
Marketing materials with trackable URLs.

faqs.question: What kinds of content can be decoded?

metadata.title: QR File Transfer - Send Files Between Devices Offline
metadata.description: Send files and text between two devices using animated QR codes. The sending screen displays a stream of codes your camera scans to rebuild the file — no network, no upload, fully offline.

qr-file-transfer.title: QR File Transfer
qr-file-transfer.description: Send files and text between two devices through a stream of animated QR codes. One screen emits the codes, the other device's camera scans them and rebuilds the file locally — no network, no servers, nothing is uploaded.

faqs.question: How does QR file transfer work?
faqs.answer: One device (the sender) displays an endless stream of animated QR codes encoding the file. The other device's camera scans the codes and the receiver rebuilds the file from them. The fountain coding used means any subset of the frames is enough — dropped frames only cost time, never correctness.

faqs.question: Is my data uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The whole transfer happens between the two screens — nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored, and no network connection is needed between the devices.

faqs.question: What is the maximum file size?
faqs.answer: Files up to 64 MB are supported. Smaller files and text snippets transfer faster, and the tool compresses the file automatically when it helps.

faqs.question: How fast is the transfer?
faqs.answer: The speed depends on the camera and the QR density. At close range with a good camera you can expect several hundred KB/s; dense frames (2953 bytes per frame) are fastest phone-to-phone at close range.

faqs.question: Is the transfer secure?
faqs.answer: The data travels only as light from one screen to the other — no network, no intermediate server. Anyone with a camera in line of sight of the sending screen could read it, so it is best for trusted surroundings.

tips: On the sender, open Transfer settings and drop bytes / frame to 1465.
Still nothing? Drop the sender's frames per second to 24 as well.
Fill this camera's view with the code, and prop the phone against something — autofocus hunting from hand tremor is the usual culprit.
Turn the sending screen's brightness all the way up.

faqs.answer: Click Generate or press the spacebar to create a random 5-color palette. If you find a color you like, click the lock icon to keep it, then generate again to randomize only the unlocked colors.

faqs.question: Can I export my color palette as CSS variables?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the Export section at the bottom of the tool to copy your palette as CSS custom properties, Tailwind config values, or a plain hex list. Click Copy Export to copy the output to your clipboard.

faqs.question: How do I lock a color in the palette?
faqs.answer: Hover over a color swatch and click the lock icon in the top-right corner. Locked colors stay fixed when you generate new palettes, letting you build around colors you already like.

faqs.question: What color formats are shown for each swatch?

faqs.question: Can I use these color palettes for my website or app?

faqs.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to generate new palettes?

css-gradient-generator.title: CSS Gradient Generator

faqs.question: How do I create a CSS gradient with multiple colors?
faqs.answer: Add color stops using the '+ Add Stop' button. Each stop has a color value and a position percentage. The gradient smoothly transitions between all your color stops in order from 0% to 100%.

faqs.question: What is the difference between linear, radial, and conic gradients?
faqs.answer: Linear gradients transition colors along a straight line at a given angle. Radial gradients radiate outward from a center point in a circle. Conic gradients sweep color transitions around a center point like a color wheel.

faqs.question: Can I copy the generated CSS gradient code?
faqs.answer: Yes. The tool generates ready-to-use CSS code displayed below the preview. Click the copy button to copy the full background property to your clipboard and paste it directly into your stylesheet.

faqs.question: How do I change the direction of a CSS linear gradient?
faqs.answer: Use the angle slider to set the gradient direction in degrees. 0 degrees points upward, 90 degrees points right, 180 degrees points down, and 270 degrees points left. You can set any value from 0 to 360.

faqs.question: Are CSS gradients supported in all browsers?
faqs.answer: Yes. CSS gradients including linear-gradient, radial-gradient, and conic-gradient are supported in all modern browsers. Conic gradients have slightly less legacy support but work in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

faqs.question: How do I use gradient presets?
faqs.answer: Click any preset button like Sunset, Ocean, or Rainbow to instantly load a professionally designed gradient. You can then customize the colors, stops, type, and angle to match your design needs.

whatIs.title: What Is the CSS Gradient Generator?
whatIs.body: The CSS Gradient Generator is a visual tool that helps you build beautiful CSS gradients without writing code by hand. Choose between linear, radial, and conic gradient types, adjust colors and positions, and get production-ready CSS instantly. Whether you are designing a hero background, a button hover effect, or a decorative overlay, this tool speeds up your workflow.

howTo.title: How to Use the CSS Gradient Generator
howTo.intro: Start by selecting your gradient type: linear, radial, or conic. Each type produces a different visual effect. For linear and conic gradients, adjust the angle slider to control the direction of the color transition.
items: Pick a gradient type using the toggle buttons at the top.
Set the angle with the slider (available for linear and conic types).
Edit existing color stops by changing their color or position values.
Add more color stops with the "+ Add Stop" button for complex gradients.
Remove extra stops by clicking the X icon next to any stop.
Try a preset like Sunset, Ocean, or Rainbow to get started quickly.
howTo.outro: The live preview updates in real time as you make changes. When you are happy with the result, copy the generated CSS code and paste it directly into your project.

tips.title: Tips for Better Gradients
body: Use two or three color stops for clean, modern gradients. Adding too many stops can make gradients look muddy. Position your stops strategically: placing two similar colors close together creates a sharper transition, while spreading them apart produces a smoother blend.

Radial gradients work well for spotlight effects and button highlights. Conic gradients are great for pie-chart-style visuals and decorative backgrounds. Experiment with angles to find the direction that best complements your layout.

items: Hero section backgrounds with smooth color transitions.
Button and card hover effects using subtle gradients.
Overlay gradients on images for text readability.
Decorative borders and dividers with conic gradients.

why.title: Why Use a Gradient Generator?
why.body: Writing CSS gradient syntax by hand is tedious and error-prone, especially with multiple color stops. box-shadow-generator.title: Box Shadow Generator
box-shadow-generator.description: Design CSS box shadows with a live visual editor. Add multiple shadows, adjust offsets, blur, and spread.

faqs.question: How do I create a CSS box shadow?
faqs.answer: Use the sliders to set X offset, Y offset, blur radius, and spread. Choose a shadow color and toggle the inset option if needed. The tool generates the CSS code automatically and shows a live preview.

faqs.question: Can I add multiple box shadows to one element?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click the '+ Add' button to create additional shadow layers. Each shadow has independent controls for offset, blur, spread, color, and inset. Multiple shadows are combined into a single CSS property.

faqs.question: What is an inset box shadow?
faqs.answer: An inset box shadow renders inside the element instead of outside. It creates a pressed or recessed appearance, commonly used for input fields, cards, and neumorphic design patterns.

faqs.question: What is the difference between blur and spread in box-shadow?
faqs.answer: Blur controls how soft or diffused the shadow edges appear. Spread controls the size of the shadow; positive values make it larger than the element, while negative values make it smaller.

faqs.question: How do I make a subtle, modern box shadow?
faqs.answer: Use a small Y offset (4-8px), moderate blur (10-20px), zero spread, and a semi-transparent black color like rgba(0,0,0,0.1). This produces the soft, elevated look common in modern UI design.

faqs.question: Can I copy the generated box-shadow CSS?
faqs.answer: Yes. The generated CSS code is displayed below the preview. Click the copy button to copy it to your clipboard and paste it directly into your stylesheet or component.

whatIs.title: What Is the Box Shadow Generator?
whatIs.body: The Box Shadow Generator is a visual CSS tool that lets you design box shadows without writing code manually. Adjust offsets, blur, spread, and color with intuitive sliders and see the result instantly. The tool supports multiple shadow layers and inset shadows, covering every common shadow pattern in web design.

howTo.title: How to Use the Box Shadow Generator
howTo.intro: Start with the default shadow and use the sliders to adjust it to your liking. The preview box updates in real time so you can see exactly how the shadow looks.
items: Drag the X Offset slider to move the shadow left or right.
Drag the Y Offset slider to move the shadow up or down.
Adjust the Blur slider to control the softness of the shadow edges.
Adjust the Spread slider to grow or shrink the shadow size.
Pick a shadow color using the color picker or enter a hex value.
Check the Inset toggle to place the shadow inside the element.
howTo.outro: To add a second shadow layer, click "+ Add" and configure it separately. You can have as many shadow layers as you need. Click the X icon on a shadow tab to remove it.

tips.title: Tips for Effective Box Shadows
body: Subtle shadows create depth without overwhelming the design. For card-style elevation, use a small Y offset with moderate blur and low-opacity black. For dramatic effects, increase the blur and offset values. Layering two or three shadows at different sizes often produces more realistic depth than a single heavy shadow.

Inset shadows are useful for creating pressed button states, input focus rings, and neumorphic design patterns. Combine an inset shadow with an outer shadow for a polished, three-dimensional appearance.

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Card and panel elevation in dashboard layouts.
Button hover and active states with layered shadows.
Input field focus effects using inset shadows.
Modal and popup depth effects.
Neumorphic UI design with combined inset and outer shadows.

why.title: Why Use a Box Shadow Generator?
why.body: The box-shadow CSS property has five values to coordinate: X offset, Y offset, blur, spread, and color. Getting these right by hand requires constant browser refreshes. This generator lets you experiment visually and copy clean CSS code when you are satisfied, saving time and reducing guesswork.

password-generator.title: Password Generator

faqs.question: How do I generate a strong password?
faqs.answer: Use this tool to create a password with at least 16 characters that includes uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. The strength meter will confirm when your settings produce a strong or very strong password.

faqs.question: Is this password generator safe to use?
faqs.answer: Yes. Passwords are generated using the Web Crypto API (crypto.getRandomValues), which provides cryptographically secure random numbers. No passwords are stored or transmitted — everything runs locally in your browser.

faqs.question: What makes a password strong?
faqs.answer: A strong password is long (12+ characters), uses a mix of character types (upper, lower, numbers, symbols), and avoids dictionary words or personal information. This generator handles all of that automatically.

faqs.question: Can I generate multiple passwords at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the Bulk Generate section to create 5, 10, or 20 passwords at once with your current settings. You can copy them all at once or copy individual passwords.

faqs.question: What does Exclude Ambiguous Characters mean?
faqs.answer: Ambiguous characters are ones that look similar in many fonts, like 0 and O, 1 and l and I. Excluding them makes passwords easier to read and type manually, which is useful when you need to enter a password on a different device.

faqs.question: How long should my password be?
faqs.answer: For most accounts, 16 characters is a strong minimum. For high-security accounts like banking or email, consider 20 or more characters. This tool supports passwords up to 128 characters long.

whatIs.title: What Is the Password Generator?
body: The Password Generator creates cryptographically secure random passwords using the Web Crypto API built into your browser. You can customize the length, choose which character types to include, exclude ambiguous characters, and generate passwords in bulk.

No passwords are stored or transmitted anywhere. Everything runs locally in your browser, and each password is generated using a cryptographically secure random number generator — the same standard used by password managers and security applications.

howTo.title: How to Generate a Secure Password
howTo.intro: Follow these steps to create a strong password:
items: Set your desired password length using the slider (4 to 128 characters). A minimum of 16 characters is recommended for most accounts.
Select which character types to include: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols.
Optionally check Exclude Ambiguous Characters to avoid characters like 0/O and 1/l/I that are easily confused.
Click Regenerate or refresh the page to get a new password with the same settings.
Click Copy to copy the password to your clipboard.

strength.title: Understanding the Strength Meter
strength.body: The strength meter evaluates your password based on length and character diversity. It rates passwords as Weak, Fair, Strong, or Very Strong. To reach Very Strong, use at least 20 characters with a mix of all four character types (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols).

bulk.title: Bulk Password Generation
bulk.body: Need multiple passwords at once? Use the Bulk Generate section to create 5, 10, or 20 passwords in a single click. All generated passwords use your current settings. You can copy individual passwords or copy all of them at once as a newline-separated list.

tips.title: Tips for Password Security
items: Use a unique password for every account. Never reuse passwords across different services.
Store your passwords in a password manager rather than writing them down or saving them in a text file.
For accounts that support it, enable two-factor authentication in addition to using a strong password.
If you need to type a password manually (for example, on a TV or game console), use Exclude Ambiguous Characters to avoid confusion.

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Creating strong passwords for new online accounts.
Generating API keys and tokens for development environments.
Bulk generating temporary passwords for team onboarding.
Creating database passwords and server credentials.

introduction.title: What Is the Unit Converter?
introduction.p1: The Unit Converter is a free online tool that lets you convert between common measurement units across five categories: length, weight, temperature, data storage, and time. Enter a value, pick your source and target units, and get an instant result with no page reloads.
introduction.p2: All conversions happen in your browser in real time as you type. The tool also shows a complete reference table so you can see your value expressed in every available unit at once.

howToUse.title: How to Use the Unit Converter
steps: Select a category tab: Length, Weight, Temperature, Data, or Time.
Choose your source unit in the From dropdown and your target unit in the To dropdown.
Type a number in the input field. The converted result updates instantly.
Click the swap button between the two columns to reverse the conversion direction. The current result becomes the new input value.
Scroll down to the reference table to see your value converted to all units in the selected category.

supportedCategories.title: Supported Unit Categories
supportedCategories.body: Length conversions include millimeters, centimeters, meters, kilometers, inches, feet, yards, and miles. Weight covers milligrams, grams, kilograms, ounces, pounds, and metric tons. Temperature handles Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin. Data storage converts between bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes, and petabytes. Time includes milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, and years.

tips.title: Tips for Accurate Conversions
tips.body: The converter uses precise conversion factors and displays results with up to 10 significant digits. Very small values are shown in scientific notation for clarity. Temperature conversions use the standard formulas relating Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin, not simple multiplication.

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Converting between metric and imperial measurements for recipes, travel, or science
Calculating file and storage sizes across different data units
Converting time durations for project planning or scheduling
Quick reference when working with international standards or documentation
Homework and study aid for unit conversion problems

faqs.question: How do I convert kilometers to miles?
faqs.answer: Select the Length category, choose Kilometers as the From unit and Miles as the To unit, then enter your value. One kilometer equals approximately 0.6214 miles.

faqs.question: How do I convert Celsius to Fahrenheit?
faqs.answer: Select the Temperature category, choose Celsius as the From unit and Fahrenheit as the To unit. The formula used is F = C x 9/5 + 32. For example, 100 degrees Celsius equals 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

faqs.question: What is the difference between MB and GB?
faqs.answer: One gigabyte (GB) equals 1024 megabytes (MB). Select the Data category to convert between any data storage units from bytes up to petabytes.

faqs.question: Can I convert between metric and imperial units?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Length and Weight categories both include metric units (meters, kilograms) and imperial units (feet, pounds). Select any combination and the converter handles the math automatically.

faqs.question: How many seconds are in a year?
faqs.answer: There are approximately 31,557,600 seconds in a year. Enter 1 in the Time category with Years as the source and Seconds as the target to see this calculated instantly.

faqs.question: Does this unit converter work offline?
faqs.answer: Once the page has loaded, all conversions run entirely in your browser with no server requests. You can use it without an active internet connection after the initial page load.

unit-converter.description: Convert units like length, weight, temperature, data, and time.

metadata.title: Regex Tester
metadata.description: Test regular expressions with live highlighting and match info

introduction.title: What Is the Regex Tester?
introduction.p1: The Regex Tester is an online tool for writing, testing, and debugging regular expressions in real time. Type a pattern and a test string, and the tool instantly highlights all matches, shows match details including capture groups, and lets you test find-and-replace operations.
introduction.p2: This tool uses the JavaScript regular expression engine, so your patterns behave exactly as they would in JavaScript, TypeScript, or Node.js code. It is ideal for developers building validation rules, parsing logic, or text transformations.

howToUse.title: How to Use the Regex Tester
steps: Enter your regular expression pattern in the Pattern field. The tool wraps it in forward slashes automatically.
Toggle flags using the checkboxes: g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline), s (dotAll), and u (unicode).
Paste or type your test string in the text area below. Matches are highlighted instantly in the Highlighted Matches section.
Scroll down to see a numbered list of every match, its position in the string, and any captured groups.
Click Show Replace Mode to enter a replacement pattern. The tool shows the result of applying your regex replacement to the entire test string.
Use the Common Patterns sidebar to load pre-built patterns for emails, URLs, phone numbers, IP addresses, dates, and hex colors.

flags.title: Understanding Regex Flags
flags.body: The global flag (g) finds all matches instead of stopping at the first one. Case-insensitive (i) ignores letter casing. Multiline (m) makes ^ and $ match line boundaries. DotAll (s) makes the dot character match newlines. Unicode (u) enables full Unicode matching for characters outside the basic Latin set.

tips.title: Tips for Writing Better Regular Expressions
items: Start with a simple pattern and refine it incrementally while watching the matches update
Use capture groups with parentheses to extract specific parts of a match
Test edge cases by including unusual input in your test string
Use the replace mode to verify that your regex-based transformations produce correct output
Check the error message area if your pattern is invalid, as it shows the exact JavaScript error

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Validating email addresses, URLs, or phone numbers in form input
Extracting data from log files or structured text
Building search-and-replace operations for code refactoring
Learning regular expression syntax with instant visual feedback

intro.title: What is a Regex Tester?
paragraphs: A regex tester is a free online tool for testing and debugging regular expressions. It shows matches in a test string in real time, and provides detailed information about capture groups and match positions. Everything is processed in your browser.

sections.title: How to Test a Regular Expression
paragraphs: Enter a pattern in the regex field and text in the test string field. Matches are highlighted in color immediately.

sections.title: Using Flags
paragraphs: Use the flag toggle buttons to enable or disable regex flags. g (global) finds all matches, i (case-insensitive) makes matching case-insensitive, and m (multiline) makes ^ and $ match line boundaries.

sections.title: Viewing Match Information
paragraphs: The match info panel shows details for each match, including index positions and capture groups. This is useful for debugging complex patterns and verifying that your regex works as expected.

sections.title: Common Regex Patterns
items: Phone number: \+?\d{10,15}
Date (YYYY-MM-DD): \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}
Hex color: #[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}

faqs.question: How do I test a regex pattern online?
faqs.answer: Enter your pattern in the Pattern field and paste your test text below it. The tool highlights all matches in real time and shows detailed match information including index positions and capture groups.

faqs.question: What regex engine does this tester use?
faqs.answer: This tool uses the native JavaScript RegExp engine. Patterns behave identically to how they run in JavaScript, TypeScript, and Node.js, making it ideal for web development testing.

faqs.question: How do I use capture groups in regex?
faqs.answer: Wrap part of your pattern in parentheses to create a capture group. For example, (\d{4})-(\d{2}) captures a year and month separately. The tool displays captured groups for each match below the highlighted results.

faqs.question: Can I do regex find and replace with this tool?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click Show Replace Mode, enter your replacement pattern using $1, $2 for group references, and the tool shows the replaced output in real time. You can copy the result with one click.

faqs.question: What does the global flag (g) do in regex?
faqs.answer: The global flag tells the regex engine to find all matches in the string instead of stopping after the first one. Without it, only the first match is returned.

faqs.question: How do I match an email address with regex?
faqs.answer: Click the Email button in the Common Patterns sidebar to load a standard email-matching pattern. You can then modify it to fit your specific validation needs and test it against sample email addresses.

metadata.title: Markdown Preview
metadata.description: Write and preview Markdown with a live split-pane editor

introduction.title: What Is the Markdown Preview Tool?
introduction.p1: The Markdown Preview tool is a free online split-pane editor that lets you write Markdown on the left and see the rendered output on the right in real time. It supports GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM), including tables, task lists, strikethrough, and fenced code blocks.
introduction.p2: Whether you are drafting a README for a GitHub repository, writing documentation, composing a blog post, or learning Markdown syntax, this tool gives you instant visual feedback as you type.

howToUse.title: How to Use the Markdown Preview Editor
steps: Type or paste your Markdown content in the editor pane on the left. The preview pane on the right updates automatically as you type.
Use the formatting toolbar at the top to insert bold, italic, headings, links, images, code blocks, and lists without memorizing syntax.
Click Export HTML to download the rendered output as a standalone HTML file with clean styling.
Click Copy MD to copy your raw Markdown text to the clipboard.
Expand the Markdown Cheat Sheet at the bottom for a quick reference of all supported syntax.

supportedFeatures.title: Supported Markdown Features
supportedFeatures.body: This editor supports the full CommonMark specification plus GitHub Flavored Markdown extensions. You can use headings (h1 through h6), bold, italic, and strikethrough text, ordered and unordered lists, blockquotes, horizontal rules, inline code and fenced code blocks, links, images, tables with alignment, and task list checkboxes.

tips.title: Tips for Writing Better Markdown
items: Use headings hierarchically: start with h1 for the title, h2 for sections, h3 for subsections
Leave a blank line between paragraphs and before/after lists for proper rendering
Use fenced code blocks with a language identifier for syntax highlighting in supported renderers
Preview your content frequently to catch formatting issues early
Use the toolbar buttons to learn the syntax for elements you use less often

useCases.title: Common Use Cases
items: Writing and previewing GitHub README files before committing
Drafting documentation or technical writing in Markdown
Composing blog posts for static site generators like Hugo, Jekyll, or Astro
Learning Markdown syntax with instant visual feedback
Converting Markdown to HTML for embedding in websites or emails

intro.title: What is a Markdown Preview?
paragraphs: Markdown Preview is a free online tool for writing and previewing Markdown text. It provides a real-time split-screen editor where you type Markdown on the left and immediately see the rendered output on the right. Everything is processed in your browser.

sections.title: How to Write Markdown
paragraphs: Type Markdown text in the left editor. Use standard Markdown syntax for formatting: # for headings, **text** for bold, *text* for italics, and [link](url) for links.

sections.title: Using the Toolbar
paragraphs: The toolbar provides buttons to quickly insert common Markdown elements, including headings, bold, italics, links, images, code blocks, lists, and quotes.

sections.title: Preview and Copy
paragraphs: The preview updates in real time in the right pane. Use the copy button to copy the rendered HTML or raw Markdown. Use the download button to save as a .md file.

sections.title: Markdown Syntax Quick Reference
items: # Heading 1, ## Heading 2, ### Heading 3
**bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~
[link text](https://example.com)
![alt text](image.jpg)
- Unordered list item
1. Ordered list item
> Blockquote text
`inline code`

faqs.question: How do I preview Markdown online?
faqs.answer: Paste or type your Markdown in the editor pane on the left side of this tool. The rendered preview appears instantly on the right side, updating in real time as you make changes.

faqs.question: Does this tool support GitHub Flavored Markdown?
faqs.answer: Yes. The editor fully supports GFM extensions including tables, task lists with checkboxes, strikethrough text, and fenced code blocks. It uses the remark-gfm parser for accurate rendering.

faqs.question: Can I export Markdown as HTML?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click the Export HTML button in the toolbar to download a standalone HTML file with embedded CSS styling. The file is ready to open in any browser or embed in a website.

faqs.question: How do I create a table in Markdown?
faqs.answer: Use pipes (|) to separate columns and hyphens (-) to create the header row divider. For example: | Column 1 | Column 2 | followed by |----------|----------| and then your data rows. The preview pane shows the rendered table instantly.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Markdown and HTML?
faqs.answer: Markdown is a lightweight text formatting syntax that is easier to read and write than HTML. It gets converted to HTML for display. This tool lets you write in Markdown and see the resulting HTML output side by side.

faqs.question: Can I use this editor for GitHub README files?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. This editor supports the same GFM syntax that GitHub uses, so your README will render the same way. Write your content here, preview it, and then copy the Markdown into your repository.

metadata.title: Image Upscaler
metadata.description: Upscale and enlarge images for free. 2x and 4x scaling with multiple algorithms. No upload, no signup — runs entirely in your browser.

guide.title: How to use:
steps: Upload an image (PNG, JPG, WebP).
Choose scale (2x or 4x) and mode (Smooth, Sharp, or Pixel Art).
Click "Upscale" and download the result.

faqs.question: How does image upscaling work?
faqs.answer: The tool enlarges your image using advanced canvas interpolation algorithms. Smooth mode uses high-quality bicubic interpolation, Sharp mode applies a sharpening filter after upscaling, and Pixel Art mode uses nearest-neighbor for crisp pixel edges.

faqs.question: Will upscaling make a blurry image sharp?
faqs.answer: Upscaling increases resolution but can't add detail that wasn't in the original image. A small, clear image will upscale well. A blurry or very low-resolution image will remain soft. For best results, start with the highest quality source you have.

faqs.question: What's the maximum upscale size?
faqs.answer: You can upscale up to 4x the original dimensions. For example, a 500x500 image can become 2000x2000. Very large outputs may take a moment to process.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. All processing happens locally in your browser using the Canvas API. Your image never leaves your device.

faqs.question: When should I use Pixel Art mode?
faqs.answer: Use Pixel Art (Nearest Neighbor) mode when upscaling pixel art, retro game sprites, or any image where you want to preserve hard pixel edges without blurring or smoothing.

faqs.question: What output formats are available?
faqs.answer: You can download the upscaled image as PNG (lossless, best quality) or JPG (smaller file size). PNG is recommended for graphics and pixel art, JPG for photographs.

image-upscaler.description: Enlarge and enhance images for free. Supports 2x and 4x scaling with multiple algorithms. No upload, no signup - everything runs in your browser.

metadata.title: Image to Text (OCR)
metadata.description: Extract text from images for free using OCR. Upload a screenshot, photo, or scanned document and get editable text instantly. No upload, no signup.

guide.title: How to use:
steps: Upload an image or paste from clipboard.
Choose an engine (PaddleOCR recommended). Optionally select a language for Tesseract.
Click "Extract Text" and wait for processing.
Copy or download the extracted text.

faqs.question: What is OCR?
faqs.answer: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) is technology that converts images of text into editable, searchable text. It works on screenshots, photos of documents, scanned pages, and any image containing text.

faqs.question: What languages are supported?
faqs.answer: The default PaddleOCR engine handles Chinese and English. Switching to the Tesseract engine supports English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Select the correct option before processing for best results.

faqs.question: Is the text extraction accurate?
faqs.answer: Accuracy depends on image quality. Clear, high-contrast text with good resolution gives the best results (95%+ accuracy). Handwritten text, very small fonts, or low-quality images may have lower accuracy.

faqs.question: Is my image uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. Both OCR engines (PaddleOCR and Tesseract.js) run entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device. Models are downloaded once and cached.

faqs.question: Can I extract text from a PDF?
faqs.answer: This tool works with images. For PDFs, first take a screenshot of the page or use our PDF to Word converter to extract text directly from PDF files.

faqs.question: Why is the first extraction slow?
faqs.answer: The first time you use a language, the OCR model (~5-15 MB) needs to download. After that it's cached in your browser and subsequent extractions are faster.

digital-signature.title: Digital Signature Creator
digital-signature.description: Create a digital signature by drawing, typing, or uploading. Download as PNG or SVG. Free, no signup, 100% private.

faqs.question: Is this a legally binding signature?
faqs.answer: This tool creates a signature image. Legal validity depends on your jurisdiction and the platform accepting the signature. For legally binding e-signatures, you typically need a service that provides an audit trail and identity verification.

faqs.question: Can I use this signature on PDFs?
faqs.answer: Yes. Download as PNG with transparent background and insert it into any PDF using Preview (Mac), Adobe Reader, or any PDF editor. Most PDF tools have an 'Add Image' or 'Stamp' feature.

faqs.question: Is my signature stored anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. Everything runs in your browser. Your signature is never uploaded to any server. When you close the page, the signature exists only in your downloaded file.

faqs.question: What format should I download?
faqs.answer: PNG is best for most uses — it supports transparency so the signature overlays cleanly on documents. SVG is vector format, useful if you need to scale the signature to any size without quality loss.

faqs.question: Can I change the color?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose from preset colors including black, navy, and dark red. The color applies to both drawn and typed signatures.

whatIs.title: What Is the Digital Signature Creator?
body: Create a digital signature image by drawing with your mouse or finger, typing your name in a script font, or uploading an existing signature image. Download the result as a transparent PNG or scalable SVG.
